## Glossary

**Account**  
A user's linked credentials for one provider (OAuth tokens or password), BetterAuth's model.

**Auth strategy**  
Frontend choice between standalone (own login) and embedded (parent frame) authentication, detected by detectAuthStrategy.

**authentication**  
Class: the BetterAuth sign-in handshake, user JWTs and their revocation, the OAuth one-time token, account changes through BetterAuth.

**Bearer token**  
Authorization: Bearer <credential>; carries a user JWT or an API token, never a session token.

**bearer-only-auth**  
CI rule: cookies and BetterAuth sessions never authenticate an API request; only withThrowawaySession builds a session credential.

**BetterAuth**  
The auth library behind `auth`: sign-up, sign-in, email verification and OAuth, mounted at /api/auth/*; used only for the sign-in handshake.

**disabledPaths**  
BetterAuth endpoints that act on a live session, kept 404 over HTTP; server calls (auth.api.*) still reach them.

**jwksStore / publicJwks**  
Signing keys in the Jwks table (private key encrypted) and the public key set served at /api/auth/jwks; keys rotate every 90 days.

**jwtHandoff**  
BetterAuth plugin (last in authPlugins) that expires the session cookie, signs the user JWT, deletes the session and answers { token, expiresAt, user }.

**meChangePassword**  
POST /api/v1/me/changePassword: a JWT route that changes the password through withThrowawaySession and returns a fresh JWT.

**oauthHandoffPlugins**  
BetterAuth plugins that mint the one-time token and move it onto the OAuth callback as #ott.

**One-time token (ott)**  
Single-use, 1-minute token in the OAuth callback fragment, consumed atomically via Redis GETDEL.

**rotateUserJwts**  
The one writer of User.jwtVersion; called by /me/rotateJwts, the admin rotation, password reset and change, and redactUser.

**Session**  
BetterAuth's handshake session: created at the end of a sign-in, at most 10 minutes in Redis, deleted by jwtHandoff; never authenticates an API request. The Prisma Session model holds no rows.

**Sign-in handshake**  
BetterAuth's sign-in flow; it ends with jwtHandoff swapping the new session for a user JWT.

**storeJwtHandoff**  
Client helper that checks a { token, expiresAt, user } answer and stores the JWT with setToken.

**User JWT**  
ES256 bearer credential, 30 days, sub = User.id, ver = User.jwtVersion; verified from its signature.

**User.jwtVersion**  
Version every user JWT carries as ver; incrementing it signs the user out everywhere. Never returned or accepted as input.

**Verification**  
Short-lived verification values such as email verification tokens.

**verifyIssuerJwt**  
The one JWT verification path: this API's keys or one configured external issuer (AUTH_ISSUER), ES256 only.

**withThrowawaySession**  
Runs one BetterAuth server call as a user through a 60-second session it creates and deletes; the only file allowed to build a session credential.

## 1. What this Warden covers

How a person proves who they are: BetterAuth runs sign-up, sign-in, email verification and OAuth as a short handshake, a handoff plugin turns its session into a 30-day ES256 user JWT, and every API call afterwards carries that JWT as a bearer header; revocation is a version bump on the user. API keys and login providers are the tokens-providers region.

## 2. The domain

No API request is authenticated by a session or a cookie (AUTH.md § Overview, CI rule `bearer-only-auth`): a person sends a user JWT, a program an API token. Sign-in is BetterAuth's handshake (§ Sign-in): `auth` in apps/api/src/lib/auth.ts runs email/password (email verification required) and Google, still creates a session at the end of each sign-in, and `jwtHandoff`, the last plugin in `authPlugins`, deletes that session and answers `{ token, expiresAt, user }` instead. The handshake session lives at most 10 minutes in Redis (`secondaryStorage`); the Prisma `Session` model is BetterAuth's schema and holds no rows. `disabledPaths` keeps every BetterAuth endpoint that acts on a live session a 404.

The user JWT (§ User JWT) is signed with `userJwtOptions` from keys in the `Jwks` table (`jwksStore`; the private key is under field encryption; `publicJwks` serves the public set at `/api/auth/jwks`) and verified only through `verifyIssuerJwt` (this API, or one configured external issuer). `jwtAuthMiddleware` compares its `ver` with `User.jwtVersion`, and `rotateUserJwts` is the one writer of that version, so sign-out everywhere (`/me/rotateJwts`), password reset or change and `redactUser` end every older JWT; there is no refresh token. An account change BetterAuth implements on a live session runs server-side through `withThrowawaySession`, called from a JWT route of our own (`meChangePassword` today; the `bearer-only-auth` fence lists its callers). OAuth ends at the API, which mints a one-time token and redirects to `/auth/callback#ott=…` (`oauthHandoffPlugins`); `AuthCallbackPage` / `completeOAuthSignIn` exchange it and `storeJwtHandoff` keeps the JWT, so neither a session nor a JWT appears in a URL. In the browser the JWT sits in localStorage (`setToken` / `getToken` / `clearToken`). The `Token`, `Account` and `Verification` model entries are listed here as auth models; how an API token works is `tokens-providers`.

Not here: API tokens (token types, owner scopes, `createToken`, the SHA-256 `keyHash`, the token lookup) and login providers (platform providers, an organization's `AuthProvider` rows) are `tokens-providers`; the middleware chain, spoofing and the `User` model are `auth-middleware-users`; the login forms, guards and auth slice are `frontend-auth`; what a caller may do is `permissions-roles`; encrypting the signing keys is `encryption`.

## 2b. Under construction

Open work you cannot use yet. Do not build against it, and do not build what it would replace without saying so.

- Session refresh: silent re-authentication, token refresh and auto-retry on 401 are not implemented — FEATURES.md § Authentication & Sessions (🟡 Session Refresh)
- SAML/SSO: schema and encryption ready, sign-in not implemented (awaiting the BetterAuth SAML plugin); the unified auth system is in progress — FEATURES.md (🟣 SAML/SSO); tickets AUTH-001, AUTH-003 (not started), AUTH-002 (in progress)

## 4. The specifics, in full

### 4a. Doc sections

Each unit is the doc section verbatim, with its headings shifted down two levels. A source line above it gives the path, the section and the doc's H1.

<!-- unit doc:docs/claude/AUTH.md#overview -->
**Source:** `docs/claude/AUTH.md` § Overview (in "Authentication")

#### Overview

Two credentials, both populate the same context. Both are bearer-only, and neither is a session: a cookie or a BetterAuth session never authenticates an API request (CI rule `bearer-only-auth`, [SCRIPTS.md](./SCRIPTS.md)).

| Credential | Who presents it | Header | Middleware |
|--------|----------|---------------|------------|
| User JWT | A signed-in user (web, admin and superadmin apps, or anything holding their JWT) | `Authorization: Bearer <jwt>` | `jwtAuthMiddleware` |
| API token | A program (MCP, integrations, CI) | `Authorization: Bearer <key>` or `?token=<key>` | `tokenAuthMiddleware` |

Both set `user`, `organizationUsers`, and configure `permix`.

Why no sessions: a session is server state that every request must look up, and a session cookie is a second way in. Sessions lived on as the real credential under an earlier JWE cookie cache, and a revoked session stayed valid in that cache for up to 7 days. A user JWT is verified from its signature, and revocation is a per-user check in Redis ([Revocation and sign-out](#revocation-and-sign-out)).

---

<!-- unit doc:docs/claude/AUTH.md#sign-in-the-betterauth-handshake -->
**Source:** `docs/claude/AUTH.md` § Sign-in (the BetterAuth handshake) (in "Authentication")

#### Sign-in (the BetterAuth handshake)

Located in `apps/api/src/lib/auth.ts`. BetterAuth runs sign-up, sign-in, email verification and OAuth. It still creates a session at the end of each sign-in, because its flows are built around one; `jwtHandoff` swaps that session for a JWT before the response leaves the API, so the client never holds a session.

##### Configuration

```typescript
export const auth = betterAuth({
  database: prismaAdapter(db, { provider: 'postgresql' }),
  secret: process.env.BETTER_AUTH_SECRET,
  baseURL: process.env.API_URL,

  emailAndPassword: {
    enabled: true,
    requireEmailVerification: true,
    onPasswordReset: async ({ user }) => rotateUserJwts(user.id),
  },
  emailVerification: {
    sendVerificationEmail: async ({ user, url }) =>
      emitAppEvent('user.verificationRequested', { userId: user.id, verificationUrl: url }),
  },

  socialProviders: { google: /* when GOOGLE_CLIENT_ID / GOOGLE_CLIENT_SECRET are set */ },

  session: { expiresIn: 10 * 60 },          // handshake only

  plugins: authPlugins(),                   // jwt(), oneTimeToken, oauthCallbackToken, jwtHandoff
  disabledPaths: [/* every endpoint that acts on a live session, see below */],
  trustedOrigins: getAllowedOrigins(),
  secondaryStorage: { get, set, delete, getAndDelete },  // Redis, `redisNamespace.session`
});
```

The plugin list lives in `apps/api/src/lib/auth/authPlugins.ts`. Its order matters: `jwtHandoff` runs last, after the one-time-token hook has read the new session.

##### What lives where

| Piece | What it is | Where it lives |
|-------|-----------|----------------|
| **User JWT** | ES256 JWT, `sub` = `User.id`, `iss` = `aud` = `API_URL`, `iat`, `exp` 30 days | The client. Web apps keep it in localStorage (`packages/ui/src/lib/auth/token.ts`) and send `Authorization: Bearer <jwt>` on every call |
| **Signing keys** | BetterAuth `jwt()` plugin keys, ES256, rotated every 90 days; a retired key stays published for 30 days so JWTs it signed keep verifying | `Jwks` table; the private key is encrypted by the template field encryption (`jwks.privateKey`, [ENCRYPTION.md](./ENCRYPTION.md)) through `apps/api/src/lib/auth/jwksStore.ts`. Public keys at `GET /api/auth/jwks` |
| **Handshake session** | BetterAuth's session for one sign-in. Lives 10 minutes at most; `jwtHandoff` deletes it as soon as it hands out the JWT | Redis (`secondaryStorage`, `redisNamespace.session`). `storeSessionInDatabase` is off; the Prisma `Session` model is BetterAuth's schema and holds no rows |
| **OAuth one-time token** | Single-use, 1 minute, stored hashed; consumed with Redis `GETDEL` (`getAndDelete`) | Redis |
| **JWT version** | `User.jwtVersion`; every user JWT carries it as `ver`, and a JWT whose `ver` differs is refused. Incrementing it signs the user out everywhere | Postgres, on the `User` row `jwtAuthMiddleware` already loads |

- **Why the signing keys use the template field encryption:** one scheme for secrets at rest, rotated by the existing `rotateEncryptionKeys` job, instead of a second scheme keyed off `BETTER_AUTH_SECRET`.
- **Why 30 days and no refresh token:** revocation is the control, not short expiry. A refresh token would be a second long-lived credential to store, rotate and revoke; incrementing `User.jwtVersion` already ends every JWT a user holds.
- **Email verification is required** for email/password sign-up; the verification email goes out through the `user.verificationRequested` app event. Verifying does not sign the user in; they sign in afterwards.

##### jwtHandoff

`apps/api/src/lib/auth/jwtHandoff.ts`, a BetterAuth plugin with one after-hook. On every endpoint that produced a new session it:

1. expires the session cookie on the response;
2. on `/callback/*` (the OAuth redirect) stops there, because the one-time token must still resolve to that session;
3. otherwise signs the user's JWT (`signJWT` with `userJwtOptions()` from `apps/api/src/lib/auth/userJwt.ts`), deletes the session, and replaces the response body with:

```json
{ "token": "<jwt>", "expiresAt": "<ISO time>", "user": { "...": "..." } }
```

That covers `POST /api/auth/sign-in/email`, `POST /api/auth/one-time-token/verify`, `POST /api/auth/sign-up/email` when verification is not required, and BetterAuth's `/change-password` called server-side by [change password](#change-password), where it first calls `rotateUserJwts`.

##### Auth Routes

`apps/api/src/routes/api.ts` mounts BetterAuth at `/api/auth/*` behind `authRateLimit`:

```
POST /api/auth/sign-up/email
POST /api/auth/sign-in/email           # → { token, expiresAt, user }
GET  /api/auth/verify-email            # email verification link
POST /api/auth/sign-in/social          # OAuth start
GET  /api/auth/callback/:provider      # OAuth callback (register as the provider redirect URI)
POST /api/auth/one-time-token/verify   # OAuth handoff exchange → { token, expiresAt, user }
GET  /api/auth/jwks                    # public signing keys
```

`disabledPaths` turns every endpoint that acts on a live session into a 404: `/token` (it would mint a JWT from a session), `/get-session`, `/update-session`, `/list-sessions`, `/revoke-session`, `/revoke-sessions`, `/revoke-other-sessions`, `/sign-out`, `/update-user`, `/change-email`, `/change-password`, `/verify-password`, `/delete-user`, `/delete-user/callback`, `/link-social`, `/unlink-account`, `/list-accounts`, `/account-info`, `/get-access-token`, `/refresh-token`, `/one-time-token/generate`. They stay 404 over HTTP. Account changes that need one of them (a password change today) are JWT routes of our own that call BetterAuth's server API through `withThrowawaySession` ([below](#account-changes-through-betterauth-withthrowawaysession)); `disabledPaths` gates only BetterAuth's HTTP router, not `auth.api.*`.

---

<!-- unit doc:docs/claude/AUTH.md#user-jwt -->
**Source:** `docs/claude/AUTH.md` § User JWT (in "Authentication")

#### User JWT

##### Verification

`apps/api/src/lib/auth/verifyIssuerJwt.ts` is the one verification path. It trusts:

- **this API**, always: issuer and audience `API_URL`, public keys read in-process from the `Jwks` table (no HTTP call to itself, no private key decrypted). The key set is cached 10 minutes, dropped when this process creates a key, and reloaded on an unknown `kid` at most once a second (another instance rotated; a forged `kid` cannot force a read per request);
- **a configured external issuer**, when `AUTH_ISSUER`, `AUTH_JWKS_URL` and `AUTH_AUDIENCE` are all set: keys from `createRemoteJWKSet(AUTH_JWKS_URL)`, cached 10 minutes.

The token's `iss` picks the issuer; an unknown `iss` is refused. `algorithms: ['ES256']` only, so `alg: none` and HS256 are refused; `iss`, `aud`, `exp`, `sub` and `iat` are required; 30 s clock tolerance. `sub` must be a local `User` id.

##### jwtAuthMiddleware

`apps/api/src/middleware/auth/jwtAuthMiddleware.ts`. A bearer shaped like a JWT (three dot-separated segments) is verified and its user loaded with `findUserWithRelations` (the cached user every request loads) → `setUserContext`. A JWT this API signed must carry the user's current `jwtVersion` as `ver`; a soft-deleted user is refused.

- A JWT-shaped bearer that fails is a **401**, never a fall-through to API-token hashing.
- Unreachable issuer keys are a **503** (retryable, so a WebSocket keeps its identity).
- A JWT is never read from `?token=`: a JWT in a URL ends up in logs and referrers. API tokens keep `?token=`.

##### Revocation and sign-out

`rotateUserJwts(userId)` (`apps/api/src/modules/user/services/rotateUserJwts.ts`) is the one writer of `User.jwtVersion`: it increments it through the scoped db client, inside the caller's transaction. Every caller below goes through it; the cache hooks drop the cached user, so the next request with an older JWT is a 401. No Redis lookup and no extra query: the version rides on the user row each request already loads. Why a version, not a timestamp: it needs no clock comparison and no second store (Aron, 2026-10-18: "the token just carries the version on the user… we just rotate that"). Permissions are not on the JWT, so a role or member change applies on the next request without revoking anything. `jwtVerify` enforces `maxTokenAge` (30 days), so no JWT, external ones included, lives longer than that. A JWT from the configured external issuer carries that issuer's version, not ours, so the version check does not apply to it: rotating here (`/me/rotateJwts`, the admin rotation, password reset or change) does not end it. It ends when it expires (30 days at most), when the user is deleted here, when the issuer stops publishing its key, or, for a `grant` JWT, when the grant inquiry is revoked (read live). Signing out at the issuer is the issuer's job. The cached user row (`findUserWithRelations`, 10 minutes) is dropped by the cache hooks on the version bump; if that clear fails (the hook logs Redis errors), an old JWT can work until the cache entry expires, the same bound a role change has.

| What | Revokes |
|---|---|
| Sign out of one browser | Nothing on the server: the SPA drops its JWT |
| `POST /api/v1/me/rotateJwts` | Every JWT this API signed for the caller, on every device: the nuclear option, not a sign-out of one device. User-only (`validatePermission(UserAction.rotateUserJwts)` on the user, `actorIsUser` in the schema): an API token cannot rotate its user's JWTs |
| `POST /api/admin/user/:id/rotateJwts` | Every JWT this API signed for that user (superadmin) |
| `redactUser` (`POST /api/v1/me/redact`, `POST /api/admin/user/:id/redact`) | Every JWT of the deleted account (`rotateUserJwts`; the soft-deleted user is refused too) |
| Password reset (BetterAuth `onPasswordReset`) | Every JWT this API signed for that user |
| `POST /api/v1/me/changePassword` | Every JWT this API signed for the caller before the change (jwtHandoff rotates on `/change-password`); the response carries the new one, or nulls on a spoof |

`jwtVersion` is never returned: every user response schema is `userResponseSchema` (`apps/api/src/modules/user/schemas/userResponseSchema.ts`, `UserScalarSchema.omit({ jwtVersion: true }).strip()`), `jwtHandoff` omits it from the sign-in `user`, and BetterAuth declares it `returned: false`, so none of its own responses carry it (a sign-up still waiting for email verification answers with BetterAuth's raw `user`). Nothing accepts it as input: BetterAuth declares it `input: false`, and no route takes a user body.

**Future: profile editing.** Profile editing will come (Aron, 2026-10-18); the write protection belongs in that route's body schema, not in a new mechanism.

- BetterAuth's `input: false` on `additionalFields` (`platformRole`, `lastLoginAt`, `jwtVersion`) only stops those fields in the request body of BetterAuth's own endpoints. It does nothing for our API routes or for server code calling `db.user.update`.
- Today nothing outside `rotateUserJwts` writes `jwtVersion`: there is no user update route, and BetterAuth's `/update-user` is in `disabledPaths`.
- A `/me` update route's body schema is the guard: accept only profile fields, never `jwtVersion`, `platformRole`, `email` or `lastLoginAt`. Email and password changes get their own JWT-authenticated routes, and a password change calls `rotateUserJwts`, like password reset does. Responses already go through `userResponseSchema`.


##### Spoofing and WebSockets

A superadmin's JWT is superadmin, so spoofing rides it ([Spoof Middleware](#spoof-middleware)). A WebSocket's `authenticate` frame carries the JWT as its `authorization` header; `apps/api/src/ws/probe.ts` replays `/api/v1/identify` with it (any credential identifies; a token is a token, with no user), and the reauthorize sweep drops an identity whose JWT was revoked or expired.


---

<!-- unit doc:docs/claude/AUTH.md#account-changes-through-betterauth-withthrowawaysession -->
**Source:** `docs/claude/AUTH.md` § Account changes through BetterAuth (withThrowawaySession) (in "Authentication")

#### Account changes through BetterAuth (withThrowawaySession)

BetterAuth already implements the account changes a person makes: changing a password, changing an email, deleting the account, linking a provider. Its endpoints for them act on a live session, and a person here never holds one. So the API keeps those endpoints off HTTP (`disabledPaths`) and calls them server-side, as the person, from a JWT route of its own.

`withThrowawaySession(userId, call)` (`apps/api/src/lib/auth/withThrowawaySession.ts`) is the one way to do that:

1. creates a BetterAuth session for the user with BetterAuth's own `internalAdapter.createSession`, living 60 seconds (Redis TTL), so a crash before cleanup leaves nothing that outlives a minute;
2. builds the request headers BetterAuth's server API reads: the signed session cookie, made exactly as BetterAuth's bearer plugin makes it (`makeSignature` from `better-auth/crypto`, `setRequestCookie` from `better-auth/cookies`). No crypto of our own;
3. runs `call(headers)`, typically `auth.api.<endpoint>({ body, headers })`. Server calls run BetterAuth's hooks, so `jwtHandoff` still swaps any new session for a JWT;
4. deletes the session in `finally`, whether the call succeeded or threw.

The session token never leaves the helper except inside those headers, and the helper logs nothing. A BetterAuth `APIError` comes out as an `AppError` (`makeError`): a 4xx keeps its status and message; a 5xx becomes a plain 500; a 401 becomes a 409 "try again", because a 401 inside the call means a concurrent account change revoked the throwaway session, not that the caller's JWT is bad. Every call gets its own session, so concurrent calls never share or reuse one.

Why not let the browser hold a short-lived session for one call (the first design): web and API are cross-site on the template's pr and staging hosts (`*.vercel.app`, `*.render.com`), where a SameSite=Lax cookie is never sent and third-party cookies are blocked, and a kept session was reachable through the one-time-token header. A server-side session never reaches a browser at all. The `bearer-only-auth` fence enforces that this file is the only one that builds a session credential: importing or re-exporting a cookie signer (`makeSignature`, `setRequestCookie`, `createHMAC`, …) from better-auth, `@better-auth/*` or better-call, a namespace import of a signer module, or any reference to `createSession`, anywhere else fails CI. The same fence names who may call the helper: importing `withThrowawaySession` (import, re-export, dynamic `import()`, `require`) outside `THROWAWAY_SESSION_CALLERS` in `scripts/ci/rules/lib/bearerOnlyAuth.ts` (today `meChangePassword`) fails CI, so each new caller is a one-line addition a reviewer sees.

##### Change password

`POST /api/v1/me/changePassword` (`modules/me/routes/meChangePassword.ts`), body `{ currentPassword, newPassword }`, response `{ token, expiresAt }`:

- **Who:** a user. `validatePermission(UserAction.changePassword)` on the user, `actorIsUser` in the schema: an API token cannot change its user's password, whatever it holds. A superadmin passes on any credential. A superadmin spoofing a user can change that user's password like any other action (no spoof guard; Aron, 2026-10-20: "Superadmin can do anything, always"); the response is then `{ token: null, expiresAt: null }`, so the spoofed user's new JWT never leaves the API, and the UI keeps its own JWT while spoofing or when the answer has no JWT (Aron, 2026-10-26: both). A superadmin cannot be spoofed ([Spoof Middleware](#spoof-middleware)), so a superadmin never changes their own password through a spoof.
- **Not in a batch:** the route is `'x-batch': false`; a batch that reaches it is refused before anything runs ([BATCH.md](./BATCH.md#routes-that-cannot-batch)).
- **Limits:** `newPassword` length comes from `passwordLength` (`packages/shared/src/auth/passwordLength.ts`, also used by the web form), the same constants `auth.ts` gives BetterAuth as `minPasswordLength`/`maxPasswordLength`; outside them is a 422 before BetterAuth runs. Rate limits: the `/api/auth` IP bucket (`authRateLimit`, 60 a minute) first, and a per-user bucket (`credentialChangeRateLimit`, 5 a minute) after the permission checks, so a stolen JWT can't guess the current password from rotating IPs and a refused token can't use up its person's attempts.
- **What runs:** `withThrowawaySession(user.id, (headers) => auth.api.changePassword({ body: { currentPassword, newPassword, revokeOtherSessions: true }, headers }))`. BetterAuth verifies the current password and hashes the new one; a wrong current password is its 400 `Invalid password`, and nothing changes. `revokeOtherSessions` deletes every BetterAuth session of the user and creates a new one; `jwtHandoff` sees `/change-password`, calls `rotateUserJwts` before signing (every older JWT is a 401 from now on), signs the new JWT through the same path sign-in uses, stamps `lastLoginAt` (the person just proved the password) and deletes that session.
- **Response check:** the controller checks BetterAuth's answer is a JWT handoff (`safeParse`); if the hook ever did not run, BetterAuth's own body (which carries a session token) fails that check and the request is a plain 500, never a leak.
- **One transaction:** the controller runs the whole call in `db.txn`. BetterAuth writes through `prismaAdapter(db)`, so the password and `rotateUserJwts` share it: if the rotation or the signing throws, the call is a 500 and the old password stands. Sessions live in Redis (`secondaryStorage`), outside the transaction; the throwaway session and BetterAuth's new one are both deleted in a `finally`, so a failed call leaves no session behind.
- An account with no password (Google only) gets BetterAuth's 400 `Credential account not found`.

##### The same pattern for the next account changes

Not built; each is a JWT route plus one `withThrowawaySession` call, keeping BetterAuth's endpoint in `disabledPaths`:

| Change | BetterAuth server call | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| Change email | `auth.api.changeEmail({ body: { newEmail, callbackURL }, headers })` | BetterAuth mails the verification link; the link's `/verify-email` finishes the change with no session. Rotate JWTs only if email is an identity claim somewhere |
| Delete account | `auth.api.verifyPassword({ body: { password }, headers })`, then our `redactUser` | BetterAuth only checks the password; deletion stays ours (soft delete, audit, `rotateUserJwts`) |
| Link Google | `auth.api.linkSocialAccount({ body: { provider: 'google', callbackURL }, headers })` returns the provider URL | The OAuth callback needs the session after the redirect, so this one must not delete it in `finally`: it needs a variant that lets the session live to the callback (as the sign-in OAuth session does) |
| Set a first password (Google-only user) | `auth.api.setPassword({ body: { newPassword }, headers })` (server-only in BetterAuth) | Same shape as change password |

<!-- unit doc:docs/claude/AUTH.md#oauth-one-time-token -->
**Source:** `docs/claude/AUTH.md` § OAuth + One-Time Token (in "Authentication")

#### OAuth + One-Time Token

Server side: `apps/api/src/lib/auth/oauthHandoffPlugins.ts` and `jwtHandoff.ts`. Client side: `packages/ui/src/lib/auth/signin.ts` and `AuthCallbackPage` ([FRONTEND/AUTH.md](./FRONTEND/AUTH.md#oauth-callback)).

##### OAuth Flow

1. **User clicks OAuth provider** (e.g., "Continue with Google")
2. **Frontend calls BetterAuth** via `client.signIn.social({ provider, callbackURL })`
3. **BetterAuth redirects** to the OAuth provider
4. **User authenticates** with provider
5. **Provider redirects to the API** at `{API_URL}/api/auth/callback/<provider>` — register this as the redirect URI with the provider
6. **API mints a one-time token** and redirects to `/auth/callback#ott=...`; the session cookie on that redirect is expired
7. **Callback page exchanges it** via `completeOAuthSignIn()`:
   - `POST /api/auth/one-time-token/verify` returns `{ token, expiresAt, user }`; `jwtHandoff` deletes the session
   - `storeJwtHandoff()` stores the JWT
   - Hydrate user data via `fetchAndHydrateMe()`
   - Navigate to redirectTo destination

##### One-Time Token Handoff

The OAuth callback is a browser redirect, so the API cannot hand the SPA a JSON body there. `oauthHandoffPlugins()` bridges it:

- `oneTimeToken({ setOttHeaderOnNewSession: true })` mints a single-use token (1 minute, stored hashed) for every new session
- `oauthCallbackToken` moves that token onto the callback redirect as `#ott=` — a fragment, so it never reaches server logs or referrers
- The browser can't mint tokens itself (`disableClientRequest`, and `/one-time-token/generate` is disabled); verify consumes atomically via Redis `GETDEL` (`secondaryStorage.getAndDelete`)

Neither the session nor the JWT appears in a URL. The one-time token resolves only to the callback's 10-minute session, and its cookie is already expired.

See [FRONTEND/AUTH.md](./FRONTEND/AUTH.md) for the client side.

---

<!-- unit doc:docs/claude/AUTH.md#who-is-a-user -->
**Source:** `docs/claude/AUTH.md` § Who Is a User (in "Authentication")

#### Who Is a User

Only a JWT session or a superadmin spoof makes the request a user (`c.get('user')`). A token never does: it is a Token actor `{ model: 'Token', record }`, and what it may do is its permissions over its owner's table. Routes name their action; there is no "is there a user" middleware.

| Credential | `c.get('user')` | `me(c)` (the `/me` resource) |
|------------|-----------------|-------------------------------|
| User JWT | the user | the user |
| Spoof (a superadmin on any credential) | the spoofed user, token set aside | the spoofed user |
| User token | none | its user |
| Any other token | none | none: `/me` answers 401 |

`GET /api/v1/identify` answers for any credential: the actor `{ model, record }` the rules see, the record being the user, or the token's own columns, without the model's redact fields.

A token held by a user (User, OrganizationUser, SpaceUser) is superadmin when its user is, and can spoof. A spoof is a superadmin and an email: the request becomes that user and the token is set aside; `spoofedBy` records who.

<!-- unit doc:FEATURES.md#authentication -->
**Source:** `FEATURES.md` § Authentication (in "Template Features")

#### Authentication

##### Person JWT (BetterAuth sign-in)

- ✅ **BetterAuth Sign-in** - BetterAuth ^1.6 runs email/password, email verification and OAuth. Its session exists only for the sign-in handshake (10 minutes at most, in Redis); `jwtHandoff` swaps it for a JWT before the response leaves the API and deletes it
- ✅ **Person JWT** - Sign-in answers with `{ token, expiresAt, user }`: an ES256 JWT (`sub` = user, `iss` = `aud` = `API_URL`, 30 days). The SPAs store it in localStorage and send it as `Authorization: Bearer <jwt>`. `jwtAuthMiddleware` verifies it from its signature; no session lookup. Details: [AUTH.md](docs/claude/AUTH.md#user-jwt)
- ✅ **Email/Password Auth** - Password hashing via BetterAuth. Email verification is required before sign-in
- ✅ **OAuth Flow → JWT** - The provider redirects to the API, which appends a single-use one-time token to `/auth/callback#ott=…` (fragment, never logged). The callback page exchanges it for the JWT. Neither the JWT nor a session token appears in a URL
- ✅ **Signing Keys** - BetterAuth `jwt()` plugin keys, rotated every 90 days with a 30-day grace, published at `/api/auth/jwks`. Private keys are encrypted by the template field encryption (`jwks.privateKey`) and rotated by the same job as every other secret
- ✅ **One Verification Path** - `verifyIssuerJwt` trusts this API's own keys and, when `AUTH_ISSUER` / `AUTH_JWKS_URL` / `AUTH_AUDIENCE` are set, one external issuer, so a JWT from a hub that issues for several apps works the same way
- ✅ **Revocation** - Every person JWT carries the user's `jwtVersion` as `ver`; incrementing it refuses every JWT signed before, with no extra lookup (the user row is already loaded): `rotateUserJwts` from `POST /api/v1/me/rotateJwts`, the superadmin `POST /api/admin/user/:id/rotateJwts`, account deletion and password reset. `jwtVersion` is never returned in a response. Signing out of one browser drops the JWT there. Revocation is the control, not short expiry, so there is no refresh token
- ✅ **No Session Endpoints** - Every BetterAuth endpoint that acts on a live session (`/get-session`, `/sign-out`, `/token`, `/change-password`, …) is disabled (404)
- ✅ **OAuth Social Providers** - Google wired via BetterAuth social plugin (callback handling, token issuance). Microsoft/GitHub are scaffolded in `platformProviders` but not yet configured in the BetterAuth client — adding them is config, not code
- ✅ **BetterAuth Models** - Verification (email verification tokens), Account (OAuth provider linkage) and Jwks (signing keys) models in Prisma. `Session` is BetterAuth's schema and holds no rows: handshake sessions live in Redis

##### Multi-Provider Auth (AuthProvider)

- ✅ **AuthProvider Model** - Organizations configure their own OAuth/SAML providers (client ID, encrypted secret, callback URL, scopes). Users authenticate via the org's configured provider
- ✅ **Platform Providers** - Providers marked `platformDefault: true` are available to all organizations. Enables centrally-managed SSO configs without per-org setup
- ✅ **Encrypted Secrets** - OAuth client secrets stored with AES-256-GCM encryption at rest. Key rotation via version tracking. Secret never returned in API responses
- ✅ **Full CRUD API** - Create, read, update, delete auth providers via API. Admin routes for platform providers, organization routes for org-specific configs

##### Token Authentication

- ✅ **Bearer Token Auth** - `Authorization: Bearer <key>` header for API access. SHA-256 hashed at rest. 10-minute Redis cache for frequently-used tokens avoids DB lookup per request
- ✅ **URL Token Fallback** - `?token=<key>` query param for contexts that can't set headers (email links, downloads). Same validation pipeline as Bearer tokens. API tokens only; a person JWT is never read from a URL
- ✅ **Hierarchical Token Scopes** - Tokens scoped to User (cross-org), Organization (all spaces in org), or Space (single space only). Scope determines which resources the token can access
- ✅ **Personal Access Tokens** - Users create named tokens with optional expiry dates. Token value shown once at creation, only hash stored. `lastUsedAt` is touched on token-cache misses only (about every 10 minutes per token), keeping a write off every request
- ✅ **Token CRUD** - Full lifecycle management. List tokens (with last-used metadata), create with name+expiry, delete by ID. Tokens scoped to the owning User/Org/Space

##### User Impersonation

- ✅ **Superadmin Spoofing** - Superadmins send `x-spoof-user-email` header to impersonate any user. Middleware resolves the target user and swaps auth context. Full access to impersonated user's orgs and permissions
- ✅ **Spoof Response Headers** - API responds with `x-spoofing-user-email` (impersonator) and `x-spoofed-user-email` (target) for auditability. Frontend reads these to show the spoof badge
- ✅ **Spoof Badge UI** - Yellow banner in AppShell when spoofing is active. Shows impersonated user's email and "Clear Spoof" button that removes the header and refreshes

##### Roadmap

- 🟡 **Password Change and Account Linking** - BetterAuth's change-password and link-social endpoints need a session, so they are disabled; JWT-authenticated routes for them are not built yet
- 🟣 **SAML/SSO** (ticket AUTH-001) - Schema and encryption infrastructure ready. Awaiting BetterAuth SAML plugin maturity for production-ready SAML 2.0 support

### 4b. Code entries

From the catalog (`.foundry/catalog/catalog.json`, extracted from the code). Each line: **name** `where` [kind] the job it does. Use: canonical usage.

#### Class `authentication`
- **Account** `packages/db/prisma/schema/account.prisma` [model] store a user's provider credentials, OAuth tokens and password per auth provider Use: db.account.findFirst({ where: { userId, providerId } })
- **Token** `packages/db/prisma/schema/token.prisma` [model] store hashed API keys owned by a user, org, space, membership or integration Use: prisma.token.findFirst({ where: { keyPrefix, isActive: true } })
- **Verification** `packages/db/prisma/schema/verification.prisma` [model] store expiring verification values keyed by identifier Use: db.verification.findFirst({ where: { identifier, expiresAt: { gt: new Date() } } })
- **auth** `apps/api/src/lib/auth.ts#auth` [primitive] configured BetterAuth instance backing sessions, OAuth and auth endpoints via Prisma Use: import { auth } from '#/lib/auth'; apiRouter.all('/auth/*', (c) => auth.handler(c.req.raw)); auth.api.changePassword(...) inside withThrowawaySession
- **AuthCallbackPage** `packages/ui/src/pages/AuthCallbackPage.tsx#AuthCallbackPage` [primitive] complete OAuth sign-in on the client callback route and navigate onward Use: import { AuthCallbackPage } from '@/pages/AuthCallbackPage'
- **AuthStrategyProvider** `packages/ui/src/hooks/useAuthStrategy/provider.tsx#AuthStrategyProvider` [primitive] supply login or embed auth strategy and authenticated state to an app subtree Use: <AuthStrategyProvider strategy={detectAuthStrategy()} isAuthenticated={...}>{children}</AuthStrategyProvider>
- **changePassword** `packages/ui/src/lib/auth/changePassword.ts#changePassword` [primitive] change the user's password, store the returned JWT and re-auth the websocket Use: await changePassword({ currentPassword, newPassword })
- **clearToken** `packages/ui/src/lib/auth/token.ts#clearToken` [primitive] remove the stored bearer token and expiry from browser localStorage on logout Use: import { clearToken } from '@ui/lib/auth/token'; clearToken();
- **completeOAuthSignIn** `packages/ui/src/lib/auth/signin.ts#completeOAuthSignIn` [primitive] exchange an OAuth callback one-time token for a stored JWT session Use: await completeOAuthSignIn(oneTimeToken)
- **detectAuthStrategy** `packages/ui/src/hooks/useAuthStrategy/utils.ts#detectAuthStrategy` [primitive] pick embed strategy when running in an iframe, otherwise login Use: const strategy = detectAuthStrategy({ parentOrigin });
- **fetchAndHydrateMe** `packages/ui/src/lib/auth/fetchAndHydrateMe.ts#fetchAndHydrateMe` [primitive] load /me user, orgs, spaces and memberships into the store and set up permissions Use: await fetchAndHydrateMe(useAppStore.setState, useAppStore.getState)
- **getToken** `packages/ui/src/lib/auth/token.ts#getToken` [primitive] read the bearer token from browser localStorage, null on server Use: const token = getToken();
- **jwksStore** `apps/api/src/lib/auth/jwksStore.ts#jwksStore` [primitive] persist and load live JWT signing keys from the jwks table Use: await jwksStore.getJwks()
- **jwtHandoff** `apps/api/src/lib/auth/jwtHandoff.ts#jwtHandoff` [primitive] swap the BetterAuth sign-in session for a JWT and expire the session cookie Use: plugins: [jwtHandoff()]
- **LoginPage** `packages/ui/src/pages/LoginPage.tsx#LoginPage` [primitive] render the login form with an optional link to signup Use: <LoginPage hideSignup />
- **oauthHandoffPlugins** `apps/api/src/lib/auth/oauthHandoffPlugins.ts#oauthHandoffPlugins` [primitive] bridge OAuth callback redirects to the SPA via a one-time token Use: const [oneTimeToken, oauthCallbackToken] = oauthHandoffPlugins()
- **publicJwks** `apps/api/src/lib/auth/jwksStore.ts#publicJwks` [primitive] build the public JSON Web Key Set from live signing keys Use: const jwks = await publicJwks()
- **rotateUserJwts** `apps/api/src/modules/user/services/rotateUserJwts.ts#rotateUserJwts` [primitive] revoke every JWT issued to a user by bumping jwtVersion Use: await rotateUserJwts(userId);
- **setToken** `packages/ui/src/lib/auth/token.ts#setToken` [primitive] save the user JWT and expiry to localStorage Use: setToken(token, expiresAt)
- **signIn** `packages/ui/src/lib/auth/signin.ts#signIn` [primitive] sign a user in by email or OAuth method Use: await useAppStore.getState().auth.signIn({ type: 'email', ... })
- **signUp** `packages/ui/src/lib/auth/signup.ts#signUp` [primitive] register a new account by email or OAuth, returning authenticated or verification-pending Use: const result = await useAppStore.getState().auth.signUp({ type: 'email', name, ... })
- **storeJwtHandoff** `packages/ui/src/lib/auth/storeJwtHandoff.ts#storeJwtHandoff` [primitive] validate a sign-in {token, expiresAt, user} response and persist the JWT Use: storeJwtHandoff(data) // after sign-in, sign-up or oneTimeToken.verify
- **useAuthStrategy** `packages/ui/src/hooks/useAuthStrategy/useAuthStrategy.ts#useAuthStrategy` [primitive] read the current login or embed auth strategy inside components Use: const { strategy } = useAuthStrategy();
- **userJwtOptions** `apps/api/src/lib/auth/userJwt.ts#userJwtOptions` [primitive] supply ES256 JWKS signing options for issuing user JWTs Use: signJWT({ ..., options: userJwtOptions() })
- **verifyIssuerJwt** `apps/api/src/lib/auth/verifyIssuerJwt.ts#verifyIssuerJwt` [primitive] verify a JWT against this API's keys or one configured external issuer Use: const payload = await verifyIssuerJwt(jwt)
- **withThrowawaySession** `apps/api/src/lib/auth/withThrowawaySession.ts#withThrowawaySession` [primitive] run a BetterAuth session-only endpoint for a user via a temporary session Use: await withThrowawaySession(userId, (headers) => auth.api.someCall({ headers }))
- **apps/admin/app/routes/_public/auth** `apps/admin/app/routes/_public/auth` [system] handle the auth callback redirect after sign-in in admin Use: apps/admin/app/routes/_public/auth (auth.callback route)
- **apps/api/src/modules/token** `apps/api/src/modules/token` [system] update, delete an existing token and read its entitlements Use: apps/api/src/modules/token (tokenUpdate, tokenDelete, tokenEntitlements)
- **apps/web/app/routes/_public/auth** `apps/web/app/routes/_public/auth` [system] handle the auth provider callback page after sign-in Use: apps/web/app/routes/_public/auth (auth.callback route)
